champion: Meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury
ordered_diagnoses: Meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury
Contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles

facts.raw_span: 7-year history of severe, mechanical, low back pain
long-standing mental depression
self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, 100 mg 4 times per day, for the past 3 years
Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the dorsum of right forearm with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure at the base
Woody induration of skin on both forearms and abdominal region
Bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
Active and passive range of motion restricted at shoulders and elbows
No signs of joint inflammation
Elevated serum creatinine kinase (192 U/L; reference range, 0-174 U/L)
Normal complete blood cell count
Shows lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates composed mainly of foamy histiocytes
Deltoid muscle biopsy showed no muscle involvement

concepts.why: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, combined with the presence of large and deep cutaneous ulcers, woody induration of skin, and lobular panniculitis on histopathology, supports the diagnosis of necrotizing panniculitis.

concepts.preferred_label: Contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
aliases: bilateral contracture of upper limb muscles
concepts.why: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, combined with the presence of bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles, supports the diagnosis of contracture of these muscles.
The patient's elevated serum creatinine kinase level, combined with the presence of muscle contracture and restricted range of motion, supports the diagnosis of elevated serum creatinine kinase.

aliases: subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes
concepts.why: The patient's histopathology results, showing lobular panniculitis with subcutaneous fat lobules and necrotic adipocytes, support the diagnosis of lobular panniculitis.

The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, combined with the presence of large and deep cutaneous ulcers and woody induration of skin, supports the diagnosis of meperidine abuse.
The patient's 7-year history of severe, mechanical low back pain supports the diagnosis of chronic low back pain.
The patient's long-standing mental depression supports the diagnosis of major depressive disorder.

rationales.F01: Chronic low back pain is a common condition, but in this case, it may be related to the patient's overall condition.
rationales.F02: Long-standing mental depression may be related to the patient's meperidine abuse.
rationales.F03: Self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine is a strong indicator of meperidine abuse and meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury.
rationales.F04: The presence of a large and deep cutaneous ulcer is a strong indicator of necrotizing panniculitis and meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury.
rationales.F05: Woody induration of skin is a moderate indicator of necrotizing panniculitis and meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury.
rationales.F06: Bilateral contracture of muscles is a strong indicator of contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles.
rationales.F09: Elevated serum creatinine kinase is a strong indicator of elevated serum creatinine kinase.
rationales.F11: The presence of lobular panniculitis is a strong indicator of necrotizing panniculitis.
rationales.F12: The absence of muscle involvement in the deltoid muscle biopsy is a moderate indicator against contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles being due to muscle pathology.
